methods.label: Special triangles and repeated rotation
methods.explanation:
The useful quantity is the angle between the diagonals, because each new card repeats the same diagonal alignment.

In the original rectangle, \(AB=1\) and \(BC=2+\sqrt3\). Choose \(T\) on \(BC\) with \(CT=2\), so \(BT=\sqrt3\). Extend \(AB\) past \(B\) to a point \(E\) with \(BE=1\). The Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
TA=TE=\sqrt{1^2+(\sqrt3)^2}=2.
\]
Also \(AE=2\), so triangle \(TAE\) is equilateral. Its median \(TB\) bisects the \(60^\circ\) angle at \(T\), giving \(\angle BTA=30^\circ\).

Now \(TA=TC=2\), and \(\angle ATC=180^\circ-30^\circ=150^\circ\). The equal base angles of triangle \(ATC\) are therefore
\[
\angle ACT=\frac{180^\circ-150^\circ}{2}=15^\circ.
\]
Thus each diagonal makes \(15^\circ\) with the long-side direction, and the acute angle between the diagonals is \(30^\circ\).

Let \(O\) be the midpoint of \(AC\). Rectangular diagonals bisect one another, so cards sharing a diagonal have the same center \(O\). This remains true at every placement. In the clockwise placement shown, the diagonal through \(B\) turns onto \(AC\), so every added card turns \(30^\circ\) clockwise about \(O\).

All vertices lie at the same distance from \(O\), since the cards are identical and rectangle diagonals are equal. Consequently, a vertex reaches \(B\) exactly when its ray from \(O\) reaches \(OB\). The smallest positive clockwise turns carrying the four original vertices to \(B\) are \(150^\circ\) from \(C\), \(180^\circ\) from the vertex opposite \(B\), \(330^\circ\) from \(A\), and \(360^\circ\) from \(B\) itself. These exhaust the four possibilities.

The first coincidence therefore occurs after \(150^\circ/30^\circ=5\) turns, when the image of \(C\) reaches \(B\). Including the original card, the total is \(1+5=\boxed{6}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
